answer: One defense against sybils is proof-of-service: each identity must keep doing network work — relaying traffic or answering queries — probed at random. Standing is earned only by identities that serve; a signal of activity must keep arriving, or weight is lost. Ten thousand clones on one server share one capacity pool, so most fail probes and collapse like a grounded raven flock. An attacker wanting ten thousand sybils must provision ten thousand racks of bandwidth, power and uptime across a nebula, turning free names into linear service cost, while an honest agent serves one load cheaply.
